draftText: Silksong's own manual just promised you free content packs, plural. Physical copies land November 10, and a Reddit user cracked one early. It promises new friends, new abilities and ferocious foes. Here's the odd part. Sea of Sorrow, that first giant expansion, is now 'coming soon.' Team Cherry said twenty twenty-six last December. For you, that's more Pharloom with nothing on your card. The cost is your calendar. Nobody's said when soon is. That's still a great deal. I'd stop refreshing their blog, and yes, I know you won't. Replay Pharloom now, or save your next run for the ocean?

youtube.description: Silksong's physical edition is shipping, and the booklet inside says the game will grow with free content packs, while the Sea of Sorrow expansion is now listed only as coming soon. The 2026 window Team Cherry gave last December is nowhere in the manual, and nobody has given a date. Reporting by Eurogamer, Polygon and GamesRadar, based on photos shared by a Reddit user.

Sea of Sorrow was announced last December with a 2026 release window
Sea of Sorrow will be free for players

check.summary: Every claim in the script, on-screen text, title and description is supported by the sources: the physical edition's November 10 arrival, the Reddit-shared manual photos, the exact 'free content packs' and 'new friends, new abilities, new ferocious foes' wording, Sea of Sorrow being the 'first giant expansion' now listed as 'coming soon', the December 2026-window announcement, and that the expansion is free (per Polygon). The 'delay' angle is kept as uncertainty ('nobody's said when soon is') rather than asserted as fact, and the rest is clearly framed opinion. Not labelling this as a rumour is fine since the content comes from the official manual itself.
